fig1_study_design: Paired design. Each schedule decodes the same (H,e,s). FRO-2 adds two only in round one; subsequent rounds use the baseline schedule. Outcomes are aggregated by key, which is the unit resampled for uncertainty.
fig2_main_results: FRO-2 lowers the observed primary failure rate across all three sampling conditions. (a) Absolute failures per 10,000 decodes; these bars are point estimates. (b) C0/FRO-2 risk ratios with archived 95% key-cluster bootstrap intervals. (c-e) Distribution of paired failures avoided per key, including all 278 key-condition units and negative and zero differences. Each key has 3,000 decodes per schedule. Improved/worsened counts denote observed differences, not individual-key significance tests.
fig3_mechanism: FRO-2 suppresses incorrect flips more strongly than correct flips, while leaving more residual errors after round one. Bars show archived absolute means; labels above each pair give FRO-2/C0. NCW denotes NCW-shallow. Each condition uses 20 keys and 1,000 errors per key. Aggregate means alone do not provide intervals; none are fabricated. Panels use separate vertical scales, explicitly labelled in their ticks.
fig4_temporal_dissociation: The effect depends on round and persistence. Upper rows show primary-point round controls with archived 95% key-cluster intervals. Lower rows show P2 (filled circles) and P3 (open squares), each with 50 keys and 1,000 errors per key and schedule, and archived 95% intervals. Shading identifies risk ratios below one, not statistical significance. Primary R2one and expanded R2-2 are separate campaigns. Primary point: (4801,45,92); P2: (3001,37,66); P3: (4001,41,82).
fig5_scope_and_boundary: Benefits transfer to an independent P2 campaign but disappear or reverse under the tested high-overlap constructions. (a) Independent P2 risk ratio, with archived 95% intervals. (b) Absolute DFR at four tested overlaps; marker offsets only prevent occlusion. NCW-aware uses exact-recovery failure, not zero-syndrome failure. (c) C0/FRO-2 and archived 95% intervals. At overlap 60 both methods fail on all trials; no resolved population ranking or degenerate [1,1] interval is plotted. The overlap axis uses actual numeric spacing; no unmeasured transition is interpolated.
fig6_threshold_window: The first round has an asymmetric two-sided response at the primary point. (a) Full six-offset absolute DFR on a logarithmic scale. (b-d) All positive offsets, separated by sampling condition on identical zero-based linear risk-ratio axes, with archived 95% key-cluster intervals. Labels give point estimates and the pale band identifies +2, not statistical superiority. Intervals overlap; marginal intervals do not establish that +2 beats +1 or +3. Connecting segments only guide the eye between measured integer offsets. Negative-offset ratio intervals remain in the complete numeric scan table; the full negative-offset failure rates remain in panel (a).
supp_failure_modes: Absolute failure-mode burden declines with FRO-2. Stacks are normalized by all decodes in each formal condition, not only failures. Segment categories use the archived preregistered quarter-budget classifier. Divergence and period-2 counts are zero in these data. All five categories were checked; zero categories have no visible area. Totals equal the formal failure counts. This campaign is distinct from the 20-key first-round-mean campaign in Fig.3.
table1_primary_summary: Compact primary table. Counts and denominators remain together; exact absolute rates are obtained by division and visualized in Fig.2a. RR intervals and Holm-adjusted key sign-test p-values use the archived formal analysis. The table carries exact inference; the figure emphasizes the effect and heterogeneity.
table1_body_main: Full manuscript Table 1: Primary comparison. All 3 data rows and all 8 columns are retained. Primary point (4801,45,92). RR = C0 / FRO-2; 95% key-cluster CI; Holm-adjusted key sign test.
table2_body_offset_scan: Full manuscript Table 2: First-round offset scan. All 5 data rows and all 4 columns are retained. Entries: RR [95% key-cluster CI]. RR > 1 favours the offset. Primary point (4801,45,92).
table3_body_temporal: Full manuscript Table 3: Temporal confirmation. All 6 data rows and all 7 columns are retained. C0 row: absolute DFR. Other rows: RR C0 / schedule. 50 keys x 1,000 errors per cell. Bold: maximum RR in each column, including ties. NCW = NCW-shallow.
table4_body_added: Full manuscript Table 4: Production-scale measurements. All 12 data rows and all 6 columns are retained. RR = C0 / variant. p: nominal exact McNemar (comparators vs FRO-2; tangent BGF vs C0). Dynamic hold-out: 3 conditions x 3 offsets; 1,000,000 trials per cell, not one pooled population. Zero-event upper bounds (3/N): 9.38e-5 per 32,000; 3e-6 per hold-out cell. Zero failures do not imply zero risk.

Method columns: DFR. p: BIKE-Flip vs FRO-2; RR: C0 / BGF-C3. Paired static semantics; 20-round budget. Tests are nominal, not key-clustered or multiplicity-adjusted.
